MAN: Can I help? Oh, you got a parking ticket!
WOMAN: Yes, and I don't understand it. I live here. On this street! Well, as of a week ago.
MAN: Yeah... I've seen you around, at the post office and the corner store. Welcome to the neighborhood! But … do you have a parking permit?

MAN: Yes. You have to purchase a parking permit in order to park on the street. We used to be able to buy them online, but now you have to go to City Hall in person. They're about fifty dollars.

MAN: Hi Jillian. What's the name of the floral company you always hire to ship flowers to your mom? I want to send flowers to my aunt, but I'm baffled about which service to choose.
WOMAN: In June, my mom got sick, and I used ShipLove to send her a get-well bouquet. It lasted over 2 weeks but was a bit pricey. So, for Thanksgiving I picked Flovely. I saved about 30 percent on the order, but the flowers died in 4 days. As I always say, buy nice or buy twice.
MAN: Thanks! I'll check both, especially their service areas. My aunt lives close to here, but in a very remote wooded area, away from the city centre. I'm wondering if they'll deliver to her home.
WOMAN: I'm sure they will-all flower businesses hire large shipping companies to deliver for them. Just make sure you place your order a few days in advance.
MAN: That's good to hear. Did you order a dozen roses, their most popular item? Next Friday is my aunt's 70th birthday, and I'd like to give her something more than just roses. Maybe a nice bouquet with a gift, but all the gifts I've researched were stuffed toys.
WOMAN: I ordered large mixed bouquets both times, but I know Flovely offers lots of gift options, like mugs, chocolates, and even paintings from local artists. They also have houseplants, dried bouquets, and tropical arrangements.
MAN: Did you say houseplants? I'd love to get my aunt a potted plant. She has such a green thumb and enjoys growing things in her garden. A potted plant would remind her of me year-round, unlike toys or a box of chocolates.
WOMAN: Another option is buying a flower delivery subscription as a gift for your aunt. That way she'd be getting fresh bouquets every week or month for a year. You'd get a hefty discount and free delivery. My neighbour ordered that from ShipLove for his wife and she was ecstatic!

M: Hey, Jude, I'm wondering if you can help me solve a mystery.
W: Sure, what's up?
M: You know how the garbage pickup comes every Wednesday morning? Well, lately, every week when I go to bring my trash cans back in at around noon, I see that a lot of my garbage has been thrown all over the place.
W: Oh, that's not good! And then you have to pick it all up. That must take a while!
M: Yes! This has been going on for some time now. I haven't noticed any suspicious behaviour in the neighbourhood, which leaves the garbage collectors as potential suspects. Although, I doubt they would toss around my garbage.
W: No, I agree, that's unlikely.
M: And I can't imagine any kids doing it. They'd have to make a point of coming over in the middle of the night or getting up early in the morning before the pickup. I suppose it's possible, but...
W: I'm thinking no. I know all the kids in this neighbourhood. How long did you say this has been going on?
M: A few weeks. Not at all during the winter...maybe just since the beginning of spring?
W: Oh! Raccoons! I'll bet raccoons are coming and going through your garbage, finding whatever they can to eat--and leaving a mess!
M: Raccoons?
W: Yes, they're about cat-sized, very fluffy, look like they're wearing a mask, and have rings around their tails. Really cute, actually, and they love garbage! And every spring, there seems to be more of them! That's why we all put our garbage out in the morning, and NOT the night before!
M: Oh! I didn't realize that! I've been putting it out in the evening, just before I go to work. I arrive back home around two in the morning, so getting up at six or seven to put it out would be like getting up in the middle of the night for me!
W: I see. Well, you could try putting heavy bricks on the lids. That works. Or, I've seen some trash cans that have a latch. Raccoons can be quite clever, so something simple might not work. You could go to the hardware store and see what they've got.
M: I'll do that! Thanks, you've solved the mystery!

Daisy, a dog owned and cherished by Deb Fitherstone, went missing Thursday night. Fitherstone had arranged for Daisy to be looked after by a neighbour. However, instead of just letting the dog out occasionally throughout the day as instructed, the neighbour took Daisy to her home nearby for some extended company.
Unfortunately, the dog wandered away. The dog is elderly, and confusion and fatigue likely played a role in its inability to find its way either back to the neighbour's house or back home. A frantic search by both the neighbour and, upon her return, Deb, was unsuccessful.
The next day, seeing the 'MISSING DOG' posters on telephone poles, Genevieve Genereau put her own dog's excellent nose to the test. While on their daily walk, Genevieve said enthusiastically to Snookums, "Go find Daisy! Where's Daisy? Where is she?"
Snookums, who did not know Daisy, did understand the enthusiasm of "Go find…!"and "Where is…?"Half an hour later, after finding several half-finished fast food meals, Snookums led Genevieve off the road into the bush to Daisy, curled up in a hole, uninjured, but unable to climb back out. Daisy and Deb were successfully reunited and Daisy is doing well.

Ellen: Let's move on to the next item on our agenda. Jane, you suggested we start a Children's Book Club. Could you tell us what you had in mind for that?
Jane: Sure. Well, we already have our Storytime for very young children. One of us reads a story and... [Seth and Ellen nod slightly] well, you both know what goes on during Storytime. The goal is to awaken a love of books. I'm thinking that a Children's Book Club could continue where that leaves off.
Seth: So you imagine something similar to a Regular Book Club? The group decides on a book, everyone reads it, and they would discuss at the next book club meeting.
Jane: Precisely. I'd even thought about having refreshments - maybe juice and cookies, or something -- but I've changed my mind on that point. I think that the books should be the joy, happiness, enough!
Ellen: Well, we don't allow food and drink in the library, so that would send a mixed signal. My concern is that there's such a wide range of reading skills and preferences among children. Do you think we should have several groups, according to age?
Jane: Yes, maybe one for the eight- to ten-year-olds, another for eleven- to twelve-year-olds?
Seth: And then we could have a Teen Club, and split that as well: one group for the thirteen- to fourteen-year-olds, and another for the fifteen- to seventeen-year-olds. That way, everyone's covered.
Ellen: Wouldn't having four different clubs add significantly to the work load? We can't afford to pay overtime.
Jane: Not significantly, no. Wouldn't half an hour be long enough for a book club meeting?
Seth: Yes, but who's going to be at the desk when you're leading the book club? We can't exactly run it as a self-service.
Jane: True enough. Well, maybe one of our student helpers would love to lead the clubs. Or maybe we could assign each club to a different student helper.
Ellen: Okay, so it sounds like we're agreed to try it, and we don't need to go to the Board for this, so...I'll approach our student helpers. Jane, could you prepare a flyer that we can put up on the bulletin board? And perhaps you and Seth could put together a list of book suggestions.
Seth: We have more girls than boys, and we want to appeal to both. Curious George comes to mind, but that might not be at the right level… Harriet the Spy would be a good choice for the older group…

parts.title: Listening for Viewpoints
intro: You will hear a presentation about television rating systems.
You will hear a report once.

sections.transcript:
Increasing concern about violence in our society often leads to a consideration of violence on television. This is not surprising since the average Canadian adult watches 30 hours of television per week; that's 4-5 hours per day. The statistics are even worse for children, who watch up to 8 hours a day.
Television broadcasters in Canada must provide a rating for most of the programs they broadcast, including American and other foreign programs, that includes consideration of the violent content in the program. The rating system, which has been in effect since 1997, indicates the intended audience age group of the program.
Some people think that simply informing people is not enough. They think that programs with gratuitous violence or, worse, violence intended to entertain, should be prohibited from broadcast. Advocates of such a change in policy refer to studies showing that viewers of such violence, especially children, may become less sensitive to the pain and suffering of others, may become more fearful of the world, and may themselves be more likely to behave in a violent way. Furthermore, refuting the catharsis argument, which claims that watching violence defuses a tendency to behave violently, such advocates point to sports events: violence increases, rather than decreases, when major sports events, which often include violence, are broadcast.
On the other hand, advocates of the status quo claim that prohibiting the broadcast of programs with excessive violence amounts to censorship. They argue that as long as people are able to make an informed choice -- and the rating system enables such a choice -- such censorship is not justified.
Television ratings systems consider not only violence, however. Sweden has recently adopted a new rating system for its televised broadcasts to highlight gender bias: to get an A rating, a movie must pass the Bechdel test (named after a cartoonist), which means it must (1) have at least two named female characters, (2) who talk to each other, (3) about something other than a man. Since its introduction, many people have been surprised to discover just how many programs fail the test.
Although Sweden's new rating system will certainly enable informed choice, it remains to be seen whether it will result in a decrease in gender bias in society at large, which is, presumably, its ultimate goal. Many people would argue that the rating system in Canada with respect to violence has not achieved its ultimate goal.

paragraphs: Dear Alex,

You weren't at yesterday's game! In all our years playing together, I haven't seen you miss a single match! I hope all is well. A few other players were home with the flu yesterday. Hopefully you didn't catch it too!

Anyways, I was wondering if you could answer a few questions for me about the entrepreneurship training program your organization offers. I heard you talking about it and it sounds like it might be just what I need. I checked out the program's website, but I still have some questions before applying.

I'll be retiring soon, and I want to start my own business. My dad used to have a floral business when I was growing up, and I've always wanted to open my own flower shop, too. However, I currently lack an understanding of how to handle budgeting. Also, does the training offer any advice on which kinds of businesses are profitable and how to create a financially sound business plan? I don't want to waste my money, so I'd like to know if my business has a chance of being successful before going ahead with it. Also, does the training include advice on how to get financial assistance? I have some savings, but not enough to cover everything I would need. I'd like to know what my options are.

According to the website, the next training session, Mondays from 1:00 p.m. to 5:00 p.m., starts soon. However, as you know, I'm a teacher, so I'll still be working full-time then. The end of the year is busy with exams, report card preparation, and parent-teacher meetings, so I have even less free time than usual. By any chance, is the program ever offered in the evenings or on weekends, or, even better, online?

My last question is about the cost. The website says fees for the training can be waived for those who qualify, but it didn't mention any further details. How would I find out if I qualify to attend for free? Are there any documents I need to send in with my application?
Thanks for any help you can give, and I hope to see you in good health next week! We play the Titans, so the coach says we'll be needing our hardest hitter!
Hope to see you soon,
Halma Sean

paragraphs: A. Riding Mountain National Park in southern Manitoba has a government designation recognizing the 1000 square miles of parkland that is home to three different ecosystems: grasslands, boreal forests, and deciduous forests. Clear Lake, the largest lake in the park, is a common boating site. The townsite of Wasagaming, the only town located in the park, is a popular summer tourist destination with quaint shops, a log cabin museum, a theatre, and a Parks Canada interpretation centre. Further enticing nature lovers to the region are a number of private cottages near the town and in the surrounding areas.

B. Riding Mountain was originally the site of a trading post established by the Hudson's Bay Company in 1741. It was there that some of the first Canadian explorers residing in the area began trading with the First Nations people. Henry Houle Hind, a surveyor for the Canadian government, documented the area's rich natural resources. Soon afterwards, the preservation of the forest became a key priority, and the logging work that had been going on was halted. Subsequently, Riding Mountain officially became a national park on May 30, 1933. The infrastructure and roads were completed in 1934 by labourers employed through Canada's depression relief programs.

C. A prominent individual associated with early conservation efforts in Riding Mountain was Archibald Belaney. He was better known as Grey Owl, the First Nations name and identity he adopted. He lived in a secluded cabin with two beavers, Jelly Roll and Rawhide. Grey Owl worked to ensure the protection of the existing beaver colonies in the parkland. Despite his efforts, circumstances for the beavers became precarious due to the drought-like conditions in the park. After 6 months of working towards saving the decimated beaver population, he was forced to find more suitable living conditions in Saskatchewan. To this day, Grey Owl's cabin is maintained as a tourist attraction.

D. Currently, Riding Mountain continues to draw from its long history. The interpretation centre strives to connect nature enthusiasts with the landscape by providing information about the area's diverse ecosystems, in addition to the ongoing work by environmentalists to preserve them. Although many tourists flock to the park for its numerous outdoor activities, like boating, golf, tennis, and camping, many are unaware of the efforts being made by local Indigenous groups, scientists, and government workers to ensure the long-term sustainability of the park for future generations.
E. Not given in any of the above paragraphs.

paragraphs: Investor Education

Canadian high school curriculum should instill more life skills in students. A number of high schools teach practical skills such as carpentry and work-related skills such as keyboarding. Some already include personal money management courses, but why not add financial investing? Teenagers who can tell a hammer from a screwdriver should also be able to tell a Guaranteed Income Certificate from a Canada Savings Bond.

The rationale is that today's young adults need strong financial skills to help them understand the concept of saving and building return on their savings. Too many parents of this generation have, unfortunately, been remiss in preparing for their retirement which means there will be little for their children to inherit. To improve their prospects, high school teenagers need to learn financial investing.

I suggested this to a school superintendent, and he said it would smack of capitalist elitism: "Our job is to graduate socially-responsible, law-abiding citizens, not to help society's top one percent increase their surplus wealth."
But shouldn't every socially responsible citizen invest in order to stave off dependence on welfare programs in old age? What's elitist about saving money?
My wife and I took up the subject with our kid's Finance teacher. Why not, my wife suggested, teach kids how to invest in an asset that grows rather than diminishes in value?

The teacher said that the curriculum, created before the era of do-it-yourself online investing, still treated investing as a specialized profession for the few rather than a personal life skill for all. "It would never fly with the parents' committee, but I'd love to assign an investment simulation. I'd have students set up a practice account at an online brokerage, research and buy a handful of stocks or funds, and see who earns the most."
"Wouldn't that be playing into a capitalist agenda?" I asked, playing devil's advocate.

"No, I think we'd be protecting them from capitalism--well, from greedy financial advisors anyway. You could present your idea to the Department of Education, you know. They are the curriculum experts."

paragraphs: I hope this email finds you well. I'm writing to recommend a book that I believe you'll find both engaging and thought-provoking. The book I'm suggesting is 'Sapiens: A Brief History of Humankind' by Yuval Noah Harari.

This fascinating work explores the history of our species, from the earliest humans to modern society. Harari masterfully weaves together anthropology, biology, and history to explain how humans became the dominant species on Earth. What makes this book particularly compelling is its ability to connect historical events to our current social and political landscape.

I recommend this book because it offers a fresh perspective on human history and challenges many of our assumptions about society, culture, and progress. The author's writing style is accessible yet profound, making complex ideas easy to understand. I found it particularly valuable for understanding current global issues in a historical context.
If you have any questions about the book or would like to discuss it after you've read it, please don't hesitate to ask. I'm always eager to share thoughts and insights about great reads.
Best regards,
[Your Name]

tasks.title: Responding to Survey Questions
scenario: Your local government is planning to build new apartment buildings near the city centre and is considering two options. One option is several apartment buildings with four floors each. The other option is one apartment building with 25 floors. The government office is conducting a survey among residents to learn their opinion.
tasks.instruction: Choose the option that you prefer. Why do you prefer your choice? Explain the reasons for your choice. Write about 150-200 words.
options: Option A: I prefer several apartment buildings with four floors each.
Option B: I prefer one apartment building with 25 floors.

paragraphs: After careful consideration, I strongly support the construction of several four-floor apartment buildings rather than a single 25-floor structure. This approach offers significant advantages for our community's development and residents' quality of life.

Firstly, multiple low-rise buildings would better integrate with our city's existing architectural landscape. The current neighborhood predominantly features mid-rise structures, and a single high-rise would create an eyesore that disrupts the area's visual harmony. Moreover, spreading the apartments across several buildings would distribute the population more evenly, preventing overcrowding in public spaces and reducing strain on local infrastructure.

Secondly, this option provides greater flexibility for future urban planning. If demand for housing increases, we can construct additional four-floor buildings without significantly altering the neighborhood's character. This modular approach also allows for phased development, minimizing disruption to current residents during construction.

In conclusion, while both options address our housing needs, the multiple four-floor buildings present a more sustainable and community-friendly solution that aligns with our city's long-term development goals.
